subject: Aurora inference disruption — findings, timeline, and required customer actions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Geller <alex.geller@aurora.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Aurora inference disruption - findings and next steps

Alex,

Thanks again for your patience while we completed our internal review of the disruption on July 4 that affected Aurora's inference pipelines.

Attached is a concise RCA appendix and a token-level service timeline. Below are the summary findings and the actions we propose:

Summary (short):
- Root cause: KV-cache invalidation after a rolling deployment triggered a backlog of cold-cache rehydration on a subset of dedicated GPU hosts, which overwhelmed our autoscaling controller and caused request queuing.
- Impact: ~6 hours of elevated latencies for the 00:00–06:00 UTC window on July 4; estimated 18% increase in median latency for affected requests.
- Immediate fix: Reverted the problematic kernel rollout and deployed a temporary eviction threshold to prevent mass rehydration.

Proposed customer-facing actions:
1) Schedule a maintenance window (we recommend Sat 07/17 02:00–04:00 UTC) for the cache warmup patch (non-disruptive, read-only warmup stage).
2) Verify monitoring: we'll share a read-only dashboard and alert subscriptions for your SREs.
3) Post-deploy verification checklist we will run jointly (see attached service-timeline.csv).

Attachments:
- aurora-rca-appendix.pdf (RCA + logs extract)
- service-timeline.csv (token-by-token timeline excerpt)

I'll loop in Vivek for the implementation details below. Please confirm whether the proposed maintenance window works for Aurora.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: aurora-rca-appendix.pdf (PDF, 420KB)]
[Attachment: service-timeline.csv (CSV, 48KB)]

From: Alex Geller <alex.geller@aurora.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2027 14:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora inference disruption - findings and next steps

Marissa,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the appendix. A couple of quick clarifications before we escalate to our engineering leadership:

1) When you say "subset of dedicated GPU hosts", how many hosts were affected and what percentage of our provisioned pool does that represent?
2) The proposed maintenance window is okay in principle, but we need confirmation that the warmup patch will not cause any downtime for read traffic. Can you confirm the warmup is non-disruptive?
3) Can you share the read-only dashboard URL and the alert thresholds you plan to subscribe Aurora SRE to?

CC'ing our Legal for awareness as there will likely be a contract/SLA review.

Best,
Alex
Head of Platform Engineering
Aurora

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alex Geller <alex.geller@aurora.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora inference disruption - findings and next steps (technical clarifications)

Alex,

Quick answers to your bullets below and a short technical plan: 

1) Scope: 14 dedicated hosts out of your provisioned 220-host pool (approximately 6.4%). The hosts were colocated in the us-west-2 placement group that handles lower-priority burst traffic.

2) Warmup patch behavior: the planned warmup is non-disruptive. It performs a read-only pre-warm sequence against pinned prefixes in the KV cache and uses rate-limited background jobs so production request handling remains on live kernels. We have run the same pattern in canary for 72 hours without P99 latency regressions.

3) Dashboard and alerts: we'll provision a read-only Grafana link with these alerts:
   - p50 latency > baseline + 40ms for 5m (severity: warn)
   - p99 latency > baseline + 200ms for 1m (severity: critical)
   - errors per minute > baseline * 1.5 for 1m (severity: critical)

Implementation plan (summary):
- Fri 07/16: final staging validation (internal only).
- Sat 07/17 01:30–02:00 UTC: pre-warm smoke run (read-only).
- Sat 07/17 02:00–04:00 UTC: progressive warmup across affected host subset; on-call SRE will watch p99 latency and abort on critical alerts.
- Sat 07/17 04:00–06:00 UTC: verification window and closure call.

We will create a Jira SUP ticket with rollout playbook and rollback steps and share it with your SRE distribution list prior to the window.

Let me know if you want more granularity on the rate-limits we plan to use.

Thanks,
Vivek
Principal SRE
Redwood Inference

Marissa, Vivek,

Thanks for the context — that helps. Two remaining items from Aurora leadership/legal before we greenlight the maintenance window:

- SLA/credit: Aurora's procurement has asked for the SLA impact calculation and proposed credit. Can Redwood share the computed minutes of unavailability or equivalent metric so our procurement team can scope the credit?
- Post-change verification: can Redwood commit to a 72-hour regression monitoring window post-rollout with a follow-up summary?

CC'ing Legal for documentation of the SLA ask. We'll confirm the operational window once we have the SLA-calculation and the monitoring commitment.

Best,
Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Geller <alex.geller@aurora.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jul 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora inference disruption - findings and next steps (confirmations and SLA calc)

Alex —

Thanks for the questions and for looping Legal. Below are the two items you requested and the next steps we will take before the proposed 07/17 window.

1) SLA impact & credit calculation (summary):
- Measured impact window: 2027-07-04T00:12:00Z through 2027-07-04T06:30:00Z.
- Affected baseline capacity: 6.4% of provisioned pool, weighted by p99 request share during the window.
- Equivalent downtime minutes (for SLA calc): 22.5 aggregate minutes across impacted routing domains (methodology in attached appendix).
- Proposed credit: pro-rated credit equivalent to 22.5 minutes at your committed monthly throughput rate. We'll provide the line-item calculation to procurement in a separate spreadsheet.

2) 72-hour post-deploy monitoring: Redwood will run a 72-hour regression monitoring window after completion of the warmup with daily summaries at 24/48/72 hours and an aggregated post-checklist at 72 hours. If we surface any regression beyond agreed thresholds we will automatically revert the warmup per the rollback steps in SUP-4321.

Operational next steps (owners & deadlines):
- Fri 07/16: Redwood to publish SUP-4321 (rollout playbook) and invite Aurora SRE to watchers list (owner: Vivek; done by 07/16 18:00 UTC).
- Sat 07/17 01:30 UTC: Pre-warm smoke run (owner: Aurora SRE & Redwood on-call).
- Sat 07/17 02:00–04:00 UTC: Progressive warmup (owner: Redwood SRE).
- Sat 07/17 04:00–07:00 UTC: 72-hour monitoring window will begin immediately after completion; daily summaries to Aurora@aurora.ai (owner: Hannah Schmitt).

Links and artifacts:
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-4321
- Read-only dashboard (will share invite before 07/16)
- RCA appendix: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AuroraRCAsample

Please confirm procurement contact for the SLA spreadsheet and whether Legal needs any additional documentation beyond the appendix. If we have sign-off, we'll proceed to publish the SUP ticket and schedule the watchers list.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
